groups.name: Chest
groups.description: Presses and flyes for the upper, mid, inner, and lower chest.

muscles.name: Upper Chest
muscles.description: The top part of the pec, trained best with incline angles.

exercises.name: Incline Bench Presses
steps: Lie on an incline bench with your hands just outside shoulder width, then pinch your shoulder blades together and drive them into the bench.
Take a deep breath and unrack the bar (with a spotter's help if needed), keeping your upper back tight as the weight settles.
Unlock your elbows and slowly lower the bar in a straight line until it touches your upper chest.
Press the bar back up in a straight line by driving yourself into the bench, pushing your feet into the floor, and extending your elbows.

exercises.name: Low-to-High Cable Flies
steps: Set both pulleys to the lowest position, attach single-grip handles, and select the desired weight.
Grasp the handles with a slightly supinated (palms up) grip and step forward into a split stance.
Keeping a slight bend in your elbows, sweep the handles up and inward in an arc, moving only at the shoulders.
Squeeze your chest as the handles meet at chest height.
Slowly lower the handles back to the starting position under control.

muscles.name: Mid Chest
muscles.description: The main part of the pec, built with flat presses and flyes.

exercises.name: Barbell Bench Presses
steps: Lie on a flat bench with your hands just outside shoulder width, then pinch your shoulder blades together and drive them into the bench.
Take a deep breath and unrack the bar (with a spotter's help if needed), keeping your upper back tight as the weight settles.
Unlock your elbows and slowly lower the bar in a curved line until it touches your lower chest.
Press the bar back up in a curved line by driving yourself into the bench, pushing your feet into the floor, and extending your elbows.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bench Presses
steps: Pick up the dumbbells with a neutral grip, rest the ends in your hip crease, and sit on the end of a flat bench.
Lie back while keeping the dumbbells close to your chest, take a deep breath, and press them to lockout.
Slowly lower the dumbbells under control until the handles are about level with your chest.
Contract your chest and press the dumbbells back up to the starting position.

muscles.name: Inner Chest
muscles.description: The area near the sternum, trained by squeezing the hands together.

exercises.name: Hex Presses
steps: Sit on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand, lie back, and hold them above your chest with a neutral grip.
Press the dumbbells firmly together so they touch along their full length.
Keeping them squeezed together, slowly lower them until they lightly touch your mid-chest.
Press them back up to lockout while continuing to squeeze them together.

exercises.name: Machine Flies (Pec Deck)
steps: Adjust the seat so the handles sit directly at mid-to-upper chest height.
Sit flat against the pad, pinch your shoulder blades back and down, and keep your chest puffed out.
Move your arms inward in a wide hugging arc, focusing on bringing your inner elbows and biceps together.
At the center, lock out your arms almost completely and aggressively squeeze your chest for 1 to 2 seconds to maximize tension.

muscles.name: Lower Chest
muscles.description: The lower pec fibers, hit with decline and dip movements.

exercises.name: Decline Bench Presses
steps: Lie on a decline bench, hook your feet under the pad, and set your hands just outside shoulder width.
Pinch your shoulder blades together and drive them into the bench.
Take a deep breath and unrack the bar (with a spotter's help if needed), keeping your upper back tight.
Unlock your elbows and slowly lower the bar in a straight line until it touches just below your sternum.
Press the bar back up in a straight line by driving yourself into the bench and extending your elbows.

exercises.name: Chest Dips
steps: Step up onto the dip station and grip the handles with a neutral grip, arms locked out.
Lean your torso slightly forward to keep the emphasis on your chest.
Unlock your elbows and slowly lower your body until your upper arms are roughly parallel with the floor.
Push through your palms to drive back up to the starting position.

exercises.name: High-to-Low Cable Flies
steps: Set both pulleys to the highest position, attach single-grip handles, and select the desired weight.
Grasp the handles with a slightly pronated (palms down) grip and step forward into a split stance.
Bending your elbows up at a 90 degree angle and close to your torso, push the handles in front of you and slightly down.
Squeeze your chest as the handles meet below chest height.
Slowly release the handles back to the starting position under control.

groups.name: Back
groups.description: Pulls and rows for your lats, upper back, lower back, and traps.

muscles.name: Lats
muscles.description: The wide muscles along your sides that give the back its width.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldowns
steps: Attach a wide-grip bar to the lat pulldown machine and sit down with your thighs secured under the pads.
Grasp the bar with a pronated (double overhand) grip.
Depress your shoulder blades, then pull the bar toward your upper chest by driving your elbows down.
Once your elbows are in line with your torso, slowly return the bar to the starting position under control.

exercises.name: Wide Grip Pull-Ups
steps: Grasp the pull-up bar with a pronated grip, wider than shoulder width.
Take a deep breath, squeeze your glutes, and brace your abs.
Depress your shoulder blades, then drive your elbows down toward the floor to pull your chin up to the bar.
Once your lats are fully contracted, slowly lower yourself back to the starting position.

exercises.name: Straight Arm Lat Pulldowns
steps: Attach a wide-grip bar to a high cable pulley and stand facing the machine.
Grasp the bar with a pronated grip at roughly shoulder width and hinge slightly forward at the hips.
Keeping a slight bend in your elbows, depress your shoulder blades and pull the bar down in an arc toward your thighs.
Once your lats are fully contracted, slowly let the bar return to the starting position under control.

muscles.name: Upper Back / Rhomboids
muscles.description: The muscles between your shoulder blades that pull them together.

exercises.name: Bent Over Rows
steps: Stand holding a barbell with a double overhand grip.
Hinge forward at the hips until your torso is roughly parallel with the floor (or slightly above), keeping your spine neutral.
Drive your elbows behind your body and retract your shoulder blades, pulling the bar toward your belly button.
Once the bar touches your body, slowly lower it back to the starting position under control.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Rows
steps: Attach a V-bar to the seated row machine, select the weight, and sit with your feet on the platform.
Grasp the handle with a neutral grip and, with your knees slightly bent, sit upright with your back straight and shoulders back.
Keeping your torso still, pull the handle into your stomach.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together, pause, then slowly return the weight to the starting position.

exercises.name: Machine T-Bar Rows
steps: Lie face down on the pad of the T-bar machine and grasp the handles with a neutral or pronated grip.
Drive your elbows behind your body while retracting your shoulder blades.
Pull until your elbows reach (or just pass) your torso.
Slowly lower the weight back to the starting position under control.

muscles.name: Lower Back / Erectors
muscles.description: The muscles along your spine that keep your torso upright.

exercises.name: Back Hyper Extensions
steps: Adjust the pad of the back extension bench so it sits just below your hip crease, then hook your ankles under the foot pads.
Cross your arms over your chest (or hold a weight plate for extra resistance) and keep your spine neutral.
Hinge at the hips and slowly lower your torso toward the floor until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings.
Contract your lower back and glutes to raise your torso until your body forms a straight line with your legs.

muscles.name: Traps
muscles.description: The muscles from your neck to mid back that shrug and stabilize the shoulders.

exercises.name: Barbell Upright Rows
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a barbell in front of your thighs with a shoulder-width, overhand grip.
Stand tall with your chest up and shoulders back.
Leading with your elbows, lift the bar straight up along your body to about chest level, keeping your elbows higher than your wrists.
Slowly lower the bar back to the starting position under control.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Shrugs
steps: Stand with a dumbbell on each side of your body, hinge down, and grab them with a neutral grip.
Stand up tall with your spine neutral and your arms hanging at your sides.
Contract your traps to raise your shoulders straight up toward your ears, squeezing hard at the top.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.

groups.name: Arms
groups.description: Curls, extensions, and grip work for the biceps, triceps, forearms, and brachialis.

muscles.name: Biceps
muscles.description: The front of the upper arm, responsible for bending the elbow.

exercises.name: EZ Bar Preacher Curls
steps: Set the seat so that when you sit down, the top of the angled pad fits snugly right into your armpits.
Place the back of your upper arms flat against the pad, keeping your elbows fully supported and aligned with your shoulders.
Grip an EZ-bar on the inner angled grooves using an underhand grip (palms up), keeping your wrists straight and rigid.
Pull the weight upward toward your shoulders by flexing your elbows, keeping your back flat and your upper arms pressed into the pad.
Slowly lower the bar back down until your arms are almost fully extended, maintaining constant tension on your biceps.

exercises.name: Standing Barbell Curls
steps: Grasp a barbell or EZ bar with an underhand grip and stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart.
Keeping your elbows at your sides, curl the weight up as far as possible.
Squeeze your biceps at the top, then slowly lower the weight back to the starting position.

muscles.name: Triceps
muscles.description: The back of the upper arm and the biggest part of arm size.

exercises.name: EZ Bar Skullcrushers
steps: Sit on the edge of a flat bench holding an EZ bar, then lie back while keeping the bar close to your chest.
Press the bar to lockout above your chest.
Unlock your elbows and lower the bar toward your forehead (or just above it), keeping your upper arms still.
Once your forearms reach parallel or just below, extend your elbows and flex your triceps to press back to lockout.

exercises.name: Cable Tricep Pushdowns
steps: Clip the EZ-bar attachment to the top pulley of the cable machine.
Grab the outer, downward-sloping angles of the EZ-bar with palms facing down.
Face the tower, step back, and hinge forward slightly at the hips. Tuck your elbows tight against your ribs, and pull your shoulder blades down and back.
Keep your upper arms locked, press the bar down towards your thighs by extending your elbows, fully locking out your arms and squeeze your triceps.
Slowly allow the bar to rise back up until your forearms are just past parallel to the floor, stopping before your elbows drift forward or the weight stack touches.

muscles.name: Forearms
muscles.description: The muscles below the elbow that control your wrist and grip.

exercises.name: Seated Barbell Wrist Curls
steps: Load the bar and sit on a bench with your forearms resting on your thighs and your wrists just past your knees.
Hold the bar with a supinated (palms up) grip.
Using only your wrists, curl the bar up toward your body.
Once your forearm flexors are fully contracted, slowly lower the weight back to the starting position.

exercises.name: Reverse Cable Curls
steps: Clip the EZ bar attachment to the bottom pulley of the cable machine and select the desired weight.
Grab the bar with a pronated (palms down) grip, hands about shoulder-width apart, and stand tall facing the tower with your arms straight.
Keeping your elbows tucked at your sides, curl the bar up toward yourself until your forearms are close to your upper arms.
Slowly lower the bar back to the starting position under control.

exercises.name: Cable Forearm Curls
steps: Clip the straight bar attachment to the top pulley of the cable machine.
Grab the bar with palms facing down, keeping the bar in front of your head, with your biceps pressed against your forearms.
Face the tower, step back, and hinge slightly at the hips. Keep your elbows tucked to your sides and shoulders relaxed.
Curl just your hands toward the floor, driving your knuckles straight down. Squeeze hard at the bottom.
Control the weight on the way up.

muscles.name: Brachialis
muscles.description: The muscle under the biceps that pushes it up and adds arm thickness.

exercises.name: Hammer Curls
steps: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with a neutral (palms facing in) grip.
Keeping your elbows tucked at your sides, curl both dumbbells up at the same time toward your shoulders.
Squeeze at the top without letting your elbows drift forward.
Slowly lower both dumbbells back to the starting position.

exercises.name: Cross-Body Curls
steps: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with a neutral (palms facing in) grip.
Keeping your upper arm still, curl one dumbbell up and across your body toward the opposite shoulder.
Squeeze at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbell back to your side.
Alternate arms with each repetition.

groups.name: Shoulders
groups.description: Presses and raises for all three delt heads plus the rotator cuff.

muscles.name: Front Delts
muscles.description: The front of the shoulder, worked in almost every pressing movement.

exercises.name: Overhead Barbell Presses
steps: Set the barbell in a rack just below shoulder height and load the desired weight.
Grip the bar with a pronated grip at (or just outside) shoulder width, step under it, and unrack it with a neutral spine.
Take two steps back, set a shoulder-width stance, inhale, and brace your core.
Tuck your chin and press the bar to lockout overhead, exhaling at the top.
Slowly lower the bar under control back to your upper chest.

exercises.name: Seated Dumbbell Presses
steps: Set an adjustable bench to 90 degrees, pick up the dumbbells, and sit with the ends resting on your knees.
Kick your knees up one at a time to bring each dumbbell to shoulder height, then rotate your palms to face forward.
Take a deep breath and press the dumbbells overhead by extending your elbows.
Slowly lower the dumbbells until your elbows are at roughly 90 degrees (or slightly lower).

muscles.name: Rear Delts
muscles.description: The back of the shoulder, important for posture and a balanced look.

exercises.name: Cable Rear Delt Flies
steps: Position dual cable pulleys at shoulder height, standing in the center.
Hold the left cable with your right hand and the right cable with your left hand.
Step back to create tension, keep a slight bend in your elbows, and engage your core.
Pull your arms out and back in a wide arc at shoulder level, leading with your elbows.
Squeeze your rear delts at the peak, then slowly return to the start.

exercises.name: Cable Face Pulls
steps: Attach both handles to a cable pulley set at about face height.
Grasp both with your palms facing each other and step back into a split stance with your arms straight out in front of you.
Inhale and pull the handles toward your face, pulling your elbows behind your head.
Slowly return the weight to the starting position under control.

muscles.name: Side Delts
muscles.description: The outer shoulder that makes your shoulders look wider.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Lateral Raises
steps: Select your dumbbells and step into an open area, holding them at your sides with a neutral grip.
Keeping a slight bend in your elbows, take a deep breath and raise the dumbbells out to the sides up to shoulder height.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position under control.

exercises.name: Cable Lateral Raises
steps: Set a pulley to the lowest position, attach a single-grip handle, and stand side-on to the machine.
Grab the handle with your far hand so the cable runs across the front of your body.
Keeping a slight bend in your elbow, raise your arm out to the side until it reaches shoulder height.
Slowly lower the handle back to the starting position, then switch sides once you finish the set.

muscles.name: Rotator Cuff
muscles.description: Small stabilizing muscles that keep the shoulder joint healthy.

exercises.name: Wall Ball Rolls
equipment: Small ball (stability, tennis, or soft medicine ball)
steps: Stand facing a wall and press a small ball against it with one hand at about shoulder height.
Keep your arm straight and apply light pressure to hold the ball in place.
Roll the ball in small, controlled circles, moving from your shoulder.
Perform circles in both directions, then switch arms.

groups.name: Legs
groups.description: Squats, hinges, and raises for the quads, glutes, hamstrings, and calves.

muscles.name: Quads
muscles.description: The front of the thigh, used to straighten the knee.

exercises.name: Barbell Back Squats
steps: Set the barbell in a rack just below shoulder height and load the desired weight.
Step under the bar and rest it across the muscles of your upper back (not your neck), gripping it wide for stability.
Brace your core, stand up to unrack the bar, and take a small step back with your feet about shoulder-width apart.
Keeping your eyes forward and chest up, sit your hips back and down until your thighs are parallel with the floor.
Drive through your heels to stand back up without forcefully locking out your knees.

exercises.name: Leg Presses
steps: Load the machine, sit down, and place your feet on the platform in a shoulder-width stance.
Take a deep breath, extend your legs, and release the safeties.
Lower the weight under control until your knees are bent to about 90 degrees or slightly below.
Drive the platform back up by extending your knees without forcefully locking them out.
Re-engage the safeties when your set is finished.

exercises.name: Leg Extensions
steps: Select the weight and adjust the seat so your knees line up with the machine's pivot point.
Sit down and position your shins behind the lower pad.
Take a deep breath and extend your legs, flexing your quads and exhaling as your knees straighten.
Slowly lower your feet back to the starting position.

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squats
steps: Hold dumbbells at your sides with a neutral grip and stand about a stride in front of a bench.
Place the top of your back foot on the bench behind you.
Bend your front knee and lower yourself until your back knee almost touches the ground beneath your hip.
Drive through your front foot to return to the starting position, then switch legs after the set.

muscles.name: Glutes
muscles.description: The muscles of the hips and the strongest in the body.

exercises.name: Barbell Hip Thrusts
steps: Sit on the floor with your upper back against a bench and roll a barbell over your legs to your hip crease (a bar pad adds comfort).
Plant your feet flat on the floor about hip-width apart with your knees bent.
Drive through your feet and squeeze your glutes to lift your hips until your torso is parallel with the floor.
Slowly lower your hips back to the starting position.

exercises.name: Cable Kickbacks
steps: Set the pulley at the bottom and attach your ankle wrap to it.
Step back with the attached leg and cross your free leg over the cable.
Pull the attached leg back at a 45 degree angle without bending your knees until it's parallel to the ground.
Slowly lower your leg down while keeping it straight and return to starting position.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlifts
steps: Position the bar over the top of your shoelaces and assume a hip width stance.
Assume a double overhand grip just outside of hip width and deadlift the weight into position at the top with the hips and knees locked out.
Begin the RDL by pushing your hips back and hinging forward until the bar is just below knee height.
Return to the starting position by driving through the whole foot and focus on pushing the floor away.

muscles.name: Hamstrings
muscles.description: The back of the thigh, used to bend the knee and hinge at the hip.

exercises.name: Stiff Leg Deadlifts
steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and the bar over your shoelaces.
Hinge at the hips with only a slight knee bend and grasp the bar with a shoulder-width, double overhand grip.
With a neutral spine, drive through your whole foot and extend your hips to stand up, keeping the bar close to your legs.
Push your hips back and hinge forward, keeping your legs nearly straight, to lower the bar back to the floor.
Reset your position before the next rep.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curls
steps: Select the weight and adjust the pad so it rests just above the back of your heels.
Tense your hamstrings to lift the weight slightly off the stack.
Take a deep breath and curl the pad down and back as far as possible, keeping your spine neutral.
Slowly return the weight to the starting position.

exercises.name: Lying Leg Curls
steps: Select the weight and adjust the pad so it rests just above the back of your heels.
Tense your hamstrings to lift the weight slightly off the stack.
Take a deep breath and curl the pad up and toward your back as far as possible, keeping your spine neutral.
Slowly return the weight to the starting position.

muscles.name: Calves
muscles.description: The lower leg muscles that point your toes and push you off the ground.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raises
steps: Adjust the shoulder pads to your height and step underneath them.
Place the balls of your feet on the platform with your toes pointed forward and your heels hanging off.
Stand up tall to lift the weight, then lower your heels until your calves are fully stretched.
Push through the balls of your feet to raise your heels as high as possible, exhaling as you flex your calves.

exercises.name: Seated Calf Raises
steps: Sit down and adjust the knee pads to rest on your quads, your heels will naturally hang off.
Extend your ankles and release the safety bar.
Lower the heels by dorsiflexing the ankles until the calves are fully stretched.
Extend the ankles and exhale as you flex the calves.
